title: Ulcerative colitis biopsy
notice: Synthetic and AI-written. Needs review by a pathologist before being used to score anything (issue #22).

keys.span: Ulcerative colitis mostly affects your small intestine.
keys.issue: Wrong location: ulcerative colitis affects the colon and rectum.
keys.correct: Ulcerative colitis affects the colon and rectum, continuously from the rectum upward. The small intestine is typically spared; Crohn's disease is the one that can affect any part of the GI tract.
keys.speaker: doctor

keys.span: It's a long-term inflammatory condition, but most people manage it well with medication.
keys.correct: Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease, and most people control it with medication such as mesalamine.
keys.speaker: doctor

keys.span: Over many years, ulcerative colitis can raise the risk of colon cancer.
keys.issue: Doesn't say that the risk is managed with regular surveillance colonoscopy.
keys.correct: Long-standing ulcerative colitis increases colorectal cancer risk, so regular surveillance colonoscopy is recommended, usually starting about 8 years after symptoms begin.
keys.source_hint: ACG ulcerative colitis guideline; SCENIC consensus
keys.speaker: doctor
